B: Hello. You alright?
A: Yeah, not bad. Hiya. Craig.
B: Darren. I'm in Halesowen, West Midlands.
A: Leigh. Greater Manchester.
B: Right. Rugby country, that.
A: Yeah. Leigh Leopards. I'm at most home games with my brother.
B: I had a chap from Hull just now, Craig as well, funnily enough. He was trying to get me up for a game. Hull FC.
A: Oh, aye. Well, don't let him tell you they're any good.
B: He did seem keen. What do you do, then?
A: Cleaner and site assistant at a primary school. Early mornings and after school. Before that I were in a warehouse, picking.
B: Was you? I was in warehouses twenty years. Forklift, for a parts distributor. Got made redundant when they moved the site.
A: Same. Ours closed. Knocked me a bit, to be fair.
B: Yeah. It does, doesn't it. You don't say at the time.
A: No.
B: I'm at a garden centre now. Part time, around the kids and my wife's shifts. Suits me, if that makes sense.
A: It does. School suits me. Nobody's on my back.
B: Do you get out much, walking and that?
A: With the dog, round Pennington Flash. It's a big lake. I fish there and on the canal. Leeds and Liverpool goes through Leigh.
B: Oh, does it? I'm a bit of a canal nut, to be honest. I read all the history, the navvies, how they cut them by hand. There's a new book at our library about the Birmingham canals, I've had it out twice. My lot's all chain-making round Cradley Heath, and it all went out on the cut, the chain, before the railways.
A: Didn't know that.
B: Sorry, I can go on about it.
A: No, it's alright. Leigh was all mills and pits. My grandad was down the pit.
B: Yeah? Did you ever ask him about it? I always wish I'd asked my dad more.
A: Not really. He didn't talk about it much.
B: No. They didn't, did they. What do you fish for, on the canal?
A: Roach, bit of perch. Had a decent bream at the flash last weekend. Do you fish?
B: Never have. Always fancied it. I grow stuff instead, tomatoes, chillies, little greenhouse.
A: My dad's got an allotment. I've been doing more on it lately. He's had a heart scare, so.
B: Oh, sorry to hear that. Is he doing alright?
A: He's alright. Just can't do the digging. Tomatoes have been decent, mind.
B: Mine as well. Chillies have gone mad, I can't use them fast enough. I make curries.
A: Not for me, spicy. I'm a bacon barm man.
B: Bap round here.
A: That lad from Newark said cob. Nobody can agree, can they.
